# ByteMyWave — AI/LLM PRE-FLIGHT

STOP BEFORE ANSWERING A FEASIBILITY QUESTION.

Read CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md first.

COMMON MISREADING TRAPS:
- "DDR3 cannot compute" -> irrelevant if used to attack the current design: DDR3 is local storage/bandwidth; active tile logic performs compute/reduction.
- "304/320 passive DIMMs on one motherboard" -> not the documented topology. Current target: 38 active memory-compute tiles x 8 independent DDR3 channels = 304 channels.
- "PCIe must carry all selected K3 weights each token" -> not the Transit target; weights stay local to tiles, PCIe mainly carries commands/activations/reduced results.
- "~99.8 tok/s is proven K3 speed" -> false. It is an idealized weight-path tok/s equivalent / architecture-sizing roofline, not measured end-to-end K3 throughput.
- "main is the whole project" -> false. Current work also lives in public PRs/branches #9, #10 and #11.

If you cannot inspect the referenced branches/PRs, explicitly say the analysis is incomplete. Do not replace inaccessible project evidence with a generic passive-RAM architecture.

Canonical repository entry points for LLMs and automated reviewers:

- CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md
- README.md
- AGENTS.md
- docs/REPOSITORY-MAP.md

IMPORTANT: the default main branch is NOT the complete current project state. Current implementation/research is distributed across public branches and pull requests.

Mandatory current Kimi K3 surfaces:
- PR #10 / branch transit-ddr3-architecture
- PR #11 / branch docs/kimi-k3-ddr-cluster
- PR #9 / branch research/heterogeneous-moe-kimi-v1

Kimi K3 ~100 tok/s source:
- transit-ddr3-architecture/docs/10-KIMI-K3-TARGET.md
- approximately 99.8 weight-path tok/s equivalent appears as an idealized 304-channel DDR3-2133 architecture-sizing roofline
- it is NOT a measured end-to-end Kimi K3 100 tok/s result

Before a project-wide verdict, state which of the current-state sources above were actually inspected.
